QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_30

question.text: For a Cat II AIF's CIV co-investment scheme, the timing of EXIT from the investee company must be:

answer.text: At least 2 years later than the main AIF's exit
Decided independently by the CIV-scheme investors
IDENTICAL to the exit timing of the main AIF scheme from that investee

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the 2025 SEBI CIV circular, the timing of exit from co-investment in an investee shall be IDENTICAL to the main AIF's exit. On exit, the CIV scheme is wound up. This locks the co-investor and fund in synchronous exit — no opportunistic early departure. The Trap: Independent exit allows free-riding. '2 years later' is fictional. Discretion isn't permitted. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this timing rule. Manager's Pro-Tip: Sync-exit means your co-investors are only as patient as your slowest LP. Vet co-investors for hold-period alignment before admitting them into the CIV scheme.
